newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 15.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Opposition members have thrown their support behind Amnuay Viravan as head of the government's economic cabinet and say the prime minister has too many advisers offering contradictory ideas. Boonchu Rojanastien, a senior Democrat, says blame for the economic ills lays not with Amnuay but with the advisory teams that can barely work together. (BANGKOK POST)

- The majority of senior military officers who responded to a survey at a seminar yesterday expressed support for the draft constitution, saying it would promote the development of democracy in Thailand. The support emerged from a poll of about 300 officers from the three armed forces, who listened to explanations by members of the Constitution Drafting Assembly. (THE NATION)

- More than 150 people representing a variety of organisations concerned with the proposed Community Forest Bill will hold a public hearing today to discuss the draft legislation. The hearing on the bill is the first one to be held under a Prime Minister's Office regulation which requires a public hearing for any government policy which will affect a large number of people so that all parties concerned can make their points down. (THE NATION)

- The Excise Department has asked the government to levy higher excise taxes on luxury products and services, a move intended to hit at the pocket books of wealthy consumers. The department has long advocated collecting such a tax, but has never succeeded in getting its wish because it ran counter to the interests of politicians and high ranking officials as well as military officers and businessmen with close ties to politicians. (THE NATION)

- Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan has taken steps to have former Bank of Thailand deputy governor and former securities exchange commission secretary general Ekamol Khiriwat participate as a member of two key Bank of Thailand working groups. (BUSINESS DAY)
